content:
maya: heads-up — observed nvme metadata write backlog spike in eu-west4 around 03:12 UTC, correlated with nightly batch and a GPU attach failure :frowning:
ops-bot: ALERT eu-west4 nvme-metadata-backlog high on hosts: gnode-12, gnode-47 (metric: nvme.meta_write_qdepth = 245) — probe started
jin: looking. can you paste the small sample of dmesg and nvme stats from gnode-12?
maya: quick tail from gnode-12:
```
[03:11:58] nvme0: metadata write latency 18ms x1000
[03:12:03] nvme0: write_qdepth 240 -> retries
[03:12:07] gpu-attach: failing to bind nvme volume: EIO
[03:12:10] janitor: starting deep-scrub job id=3212
```
sam: ⬆️ that janitor deep-scrub is suspicious — it started exactly when batch kicked off. scrub was supposed to be in the 02:00 window for eu-west4, but looks shifted.
lee: checked scheduling logs — scrub cadence drifted because the last maintenance run bumped leader lease to a different controller. scrub-window variable reset failed.
anika: can we just pause the deep-scrub for the region until we stabilize? cost of pause is negligible vs attaching failing GPUs.
jin: agree. proposal:
- pause janitor deep-scrub for eu-west4 (only metadata deep-scrub tasks)
- temporarily tighten scrub concurrency to 2
- bump nvme metadata writeback throttle to avoid qdepth spikes
- run targeted reclaim on hot gnodes
maya: sounds good. what's the safest command to pause without causing backlog growth? don't want to drop records.
jin: run the operator flag to transition gracefully:
```
kubectl -n infra patch cronjob janitor-deep-scrub-eu-west4 -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'
```
then scale the janitor workers:
```
kubectl -n infra scale deployment janitor-worker --replicas=2 -l region=eu-west4
```
sam: I'll apply that now and watch attach logs.
ops-bot: ACTION start: pause deep-scrub eu-west4 by sam at 03:17 UTC
sam: applied patch + scaled workers.
sam: immediate drop in nvme.meta_write_qdepth on gnode-12: 245 -> 42 within 90s :thumbsup:
maya: GPU attach succeeded for two pending jobs, attaching backlog cleared.
jin: follow-up: we should fix the scrub scheduling leader bug. filing a short-term mitigation patch to pin scrub-controller leader to zone-affine pod in eu-west4-primary.
lee: created PR #4578 with leader-affinity fix and a health-check that reclaims drifted leases. also added a metric alert for scrub-start-time drift.
anika: ops ask: is there any data corruption risk from pausing scrub? will we need a catch-up plan?
jin: low risk — this is metadata deep-scrub (consistency checks); pausing delays verification but doesn't drop metadata. we'll run a catch-up with reduced concurrency later during low-traffic window.
maya: cost note — this avoided re-provisioning a handful of GPUs in eu-west4, probably saved ~2k USD/week in emergency moves. please add to incident cost tracker.
ops-bot: NOTE job: collect nvme metrics and attach logs between 03:00-04:00 UTC for postmortem.
sam: I'll collate logs and drop in #postmortems after the PR lands.
lee: quick TODOs:
- merge #4578 (lee)
- schedule catch-up scrub for 04:30 UTC with concurrency=1 (sam)
- monitor nvme.meta_write_qdepth for 6 hours (maya)
- add runbook note about pausing deep-scrub for GPU attach events (jin)
maya: thanks team — keeping an eye. will ping if anything flares back up :eyes:
ops-bot: ACTION complete: pause deep-scrub eu-west4 by sam at 03:20 UTC
